messages:
leo (sdk): starting canary rollout of sdk-server v5.1 to 5% now — includes rate-limit header rename and a tiny streaming frame change. watching logs and metrics. 2312305555

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout v5.1 -> subset=5% (canary). CID: dpl-9f3a. 2312305560

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: increase in 429s for /v1/stream in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. 1m spike: +420% errors. Pager threshold breached. 2312305605

alex (sre): seeing client reconnect loops on streaming endpoints, repeated frame decode failures in logs: `stream_frame: invalid_header_len`. Also seeing burst of 429s coming from our edge LB — looks correlated with canary traffic. 2312305612

maya (infra): pulling traces. Preliminary: new `X-RW-Quota` header may cause some rate-limit middleware to misclassify tokens — but more likely the streaming frame change changed the first byte marker for older clients. Quick check: 95% of errors are from SDKs older than v5.0. 2312305620

leo (sdk): ack. The change set included a small header ordering change plus a `frame_type` byte tweak to optimize decode. We expected backwards compatible, but maybe older clients assume a zeroed reserved byte. rolling FF off path available? 2312305630

raja (pm): how many customers impacted? any enterprise SLA at risk? 2312305642

ian (cs): CS dashboards show 7 customers with repeated disconnects; 3 are enterprise (two in EU, one in APAC). At least one opened a support ticket complaining of timeouts during live demos. We should prioritize mitigation. 2312305655

alex (sre): mitigation plan: 1) kill canary via feature flag 2) if FF not enough, rollback to v5.0 3) increase rate-limit thresholds temporarily to cut 429 noise. Can someone flip the FF? 2312305668

maya (infra): flipping flag now: `rw-ffctl set sdk-streaming-canary=false --env=prod` 2312305675

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: sdk-streaming-canary=false by maya (infra). Change applied to proxy routing layer. 2312305680

alex (sre): monitoring — still seeing error tail, likely because a portion of traffic is pinned to canary nodes. initiating rollback of v5.1 canary nodes. 2312305690

leo (sdk): do a staged rollback, please. If we quick rollback, ensure we don't double-throttle clients. 2312305695

deploy-bot: Initiating rollback: rollback v5.1 -> v5.0 on canary subset. Command: `dpl rollback dpl-9f3a --subset=canary`. 2312305702

deploy-bot: Rollback progress: terminating canary pods (3/3), routing traffic back to stable. 2312305760

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. All traffic routed to v5.0. 2312305785

alex (sre): good — error rates dropping but there's a residual spike from client reconnect storms. I'm going to temporarily bump token bucket for streaming ingress for 10m to let stuck clients reconnect gracefully: `rw-lb adjust-rate --name=stream_ingress --burst=3x --duration=10m`. 2312305798

maya (infra): bumped rate-limit burst for streaming ingress. Watch for downstream overload. 2312305810

ian (cs): customers reporting improvement, some sessions resumed. Ticket owners notified of rollback; providing postmortem note. 2312305825

raja (pm): quick customer impact summary for execs: approx 7 customers affected, 3 enterprise, duration ~20-30m with disconnects/timeouts, mitigated via FF kill + rollback. Would like a short blameless postmortem and next steps. 2312305833

leo (sdk): root cause hypothesis: v5.1 introduced a subtle streaming frame header tweak that older SDKs assume zeroed reserved byte for backward-compatibility. We missed a compatibility test in our canary matrix (didn't include pre-1.8 clients). Will prepare reproducible test and patch. 2312305845

alex (sre): actions captured: 1) incident thread + postmortem (owner: leo) 2) add compatibility test to canary matrix (owner: leo + maya) 3) add runtime check to reject unknown frame formats with clearer metrics (owner: alex) 4) communicate to affected customers (owner: ian) 2312305860

rachel (oncall): taking handoff for the 23:00-07:00 shift. I have context and will follow up on monitoring and postmortem items. If anything flares, page me. :thumbsup: 2312305875

incident-bot: Incident logged: INC-2023-231230-canary-rlimit. Severity: P2. Assigned: leo (sdk), alex (sre), ian (cs). 2312305880
